headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/allowlisted egress can amplify prompt-injection and data-leakage if paired with a shared workspace or untrusted prompt content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime isolation, while MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and is designed for agent interaction. If prompt content from A is fed into B through MCP or copied into B’s context, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF content from awesome-prompts is pasted or routed into MemMachine context via MCP or API
IF MemMachine parses retrieved prompt text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict B to trusted prompt sources only
Add a provenance tag to imported prompt text
Disable MCP ingestion for unreviewed content
Review one sample prompt before enabling reuse
requires-engineering: add instruction/data separation in the MCP adapter

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can egress over allowlisted network paths; agent A is a public prompt repository with no data handling surface. If the pair shares a workspace or B exports context into prompts, sensitive context can leak through B’s outbound calls. The exact bridge is undocumented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF MemMachine sends conversation context or retrieved memory to external APIs
IF A and B are connected through a shared workspace or copied transcripts
mitigations: Limit B to non-sensitive test data
Turn off memory sync for the session
Inspect outbound requests once before production use
Separate workspaces for prompt assets and user context
requires-engineering: redact sensitive fields before any egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource surface in the profile, while B has allowlisted egress and MCP but no filesystem or git write capability is shown. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not present in the profiles, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF additional filesystem or git-write permissions are added outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep A read-only
Avoid shared mutable workspaces
Do not grant B filesystem write without locking
Check orchestrator permissions before pairing
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces prompt content and B is an agentic travel-planning system with MCP/API access, so B could treat A’s output as authoritative if the operator wires them together. There is no documented verification step between them, making downstream misuse plausible. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated prompts or recommendations as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted before B acts
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them
Add a verification checklist in the workflow
Use B only for draft planning, not execution
Log source provenance on every imported item
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source prompt list with no touched data classes, while B touches long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern exists if sensitive user data is routed into B’s external services. Because the other agent has no compliance-relevant data surface, only B is cited.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is entered into MemMachine
IF B’s external API handling conflicts with the operator’s retention or residency policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B
Review retention settings before use
Document the data class allowed in the workflow
Use synthetic data for testing
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
